raw_text:
Perfect, but the rendering is now a bit weird because we show the app list and then we show also the workspaces if there are any. But an app has an app instance.

So I would propose to change the display of the app lists to become instead of in a table use a data list component. an then show columns

- Name
- repo
- Instances (count)
- Workspaces (count across instances)

Then when you click through on an application, you could see the where which instances it is deployed, and also the workspaces, and that can be shown in a table view. That could be similar to the current app list view in the table, where we just display the instances, and then the worktree breakdown underneath each instance. And then we can also add a column whether the dependencies are okay or not, because we can check dependencies audits. And we could also perhaps show the URL for each instance and workspace, like we have now in the app list.

expectation: Keep logical app inventory separate from placement drill-down and preserve placement-scoped visibility.

protection.rejected_example: app:list mixes logical apps and workspace child rows in one table, while app:show authorizes only through default-node metadata.
protection.accepted_example: app:list renders repository plus visible counts in a DataList, and app:show renders visible instances with nested workspace URLs and app-scoped dependency posture.
